I wrote `summary.csv` to `/tmp/psz-work/r1a/t2_expenses/stock/0/summary.csv`:

```
month,category,total_eur
2026-10,maaltijden,18.75
2026-10,reizen,32.70
2026-10,software,53.36
2026-11,maaltijden,32.05
2026-11,reizen,179.28
2026-11,software,14.71
```

How the numbers were derived:
- **Duplicates:** E02 appears twice in the file, and E09 appears twice. Each was counted once.
- **Excluded:** E04 and E11 (category `privé`).
- **Refund:** E06 (−12,50 EUR) is subtracted from October reizen.
- **USD conversion at 0.92:** E02 and E03 are 29.00 USD each, giving 26.68 EUR each. E08 is 15.99 USD, giving 14.7108 EUR. E12 is 64.00 USD, giving 58.88 EUR.
- **Rounding:** Only the final totals were rounded, half up. The only one that needed it was November software, 14.7108, which became 14.71.

One thing to check: E12 is dated 2026-11-27, which is after today's date (2026-11-25). I included it because the rules don't exclude future-dated rows. If it shouldn't be there, November reizen becomes 120.40 and the file needs one row changed.
